title: How would you estimate how many hairdressers work in London?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How many hairdressers work in London?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: A classic supply-and-demand sizing: work out how many haircuts London needs, then how many one hairdresser can give. Have a go at your own estimate before reading on.
body:
The question

How many hairdressers work in London?

The approach

Haircuts needed per year ÷ haircuts one hairdresser can do per year.

Tip: Write each step with its unit, so you never lose track of whether you are counting people, homes or purchases.

Step by step

  1. People in London: 9M
  2. × 6 haircuts each per year
  3. ÷ 2,112 haircuts per hairdresser per year (8 a day, 5.5 days, 48 weeks)

That gives about 25.6k hairdressers.

Does it make sense?

Roughly one hairdresser per 350 Londoners, about one salon chair per few streets.

Demand is not the same as the number of people employed

The original estimate gives about 25,600 full-time-equivalent hairdressers under its assumptions. But the interviewer may ask for individual workers, and some hairdressers work part time. If the average worker provides only 75% of the assumed full-time hours, 25,600 full-time equivalents translate into roughly 34,100 individual workers.

Check the other side of the equation: 9 million residents receiving six cuts a year means 54 million haircuts. If the average service takes 45 minutes, that represents about 40.5 million chair-hours before time spent colouring, styling, cleaning and waiting. A business that sells more complex appointments can serve fewer clients per day.

State whether you include barbers, salon apprentices, mobile stylists and haircuts bought by commuters or tourists. The way you define the service can matter as much as the arithmetic.
